proof:
Source (provenance only): step 3 of the parent proof (separation (b)), with Q written as (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∩ {δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖} = (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∖ B̆_δ(v₀) and ε₀ chosen so that B_{ε₀}(x) ⊆ W; only continuity of φ on V, injectivity of φ on V and the properness hypothesis are used, and V need not be open.
Notation: x := φ(v₀); B_ρ(p) is the closed ball and B̆_ρ(p) the open ball. Fix δ > 0.
1. Choice of ε₀. W is open and x ∈ W, so there is ε₁ > 0 with B̆_{ε₁}(x) ⊆ W (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put ε₀ := ε₁/2 > 0. Then K₀ := B_{ε₀}(x) ⊆ B̆_{ε₁}(x) ⊆ W (closedBall_subset_ball), and K₀ is compact (isCompact_closedBall; ℝ^N is proper).
2. The compact set Q. By the properness hypothesis applied to K₀, the set V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀) is compact. The set D := {v ∈ ℝᵐ : δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖} is closed (isClosed_le of two continuous functions). Hence Q := (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∩ D is compact (IsCompact.inter_right). Since Q ⊆ V and φ is continuous on V, the function v ↦ ‖φ(v) − x‖ is continuous on Q.
3. Case Q ≠ ∅. A continuous function on a nonempty compact set attains its minimum (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn): there is q ∈ Q with ‖φ(q) − x‖ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖ for every v ∈ Q. Moreover ‖φ(q) − x‖ > 0: otherwise φ(q) = φ(v₀) with q ∈ V and v₀ ∈ V, so q = v₀ by injectivity of φ on V, and then δ ≤ ‖q − v₀‖ = 0 contradicts δ > 0. Put ε := min(ε₀, ‖φ(q) − x‖) > 0. Let v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖. If φ(v) ∈ K₀, then v ∈ Q, so ε ≤ ‖φ(q) − x‖ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖. If φ(v) ∉ K₀, then ‖φ(v) − x‖ > ε₀ ≥ ε.
4. Case Q = ∅. Put ε := ε₀ > 0. Let v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖. If ‖φ(v) − x‖ < ε₀, then φ(v) ∈ K₀, so v ∈ Q, which is impossible. Hence ε = ε₀ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖.
5. In both cases ε > 0 and ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ for every v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖.
key_steps: a closed ball K₀ = B_{ε₀}(φ(v₀)) ⊆ W, compact
Q = (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∩ {v : δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖} is compact by properness
the minimum of ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ on Q (if Q ≠ ∅) is positive by injectivity on V
ε := min(ε₀, that minimum), or ε₀ if Q = ∅; points with φ(v) ∉ K₀ are farther than ε₀
